project_updates.title: Campus chronology and investment phases remain distinct
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: South Carolina Commerce and Governor releases, Google location pages, and contemporaneous expansion announcements for 2006-2026. Queries: Google Berkeley County, Mount Holly Commerce Park, Maguro Enterprises, Project Eagle, Project Linden, expansion, investment, operational, and second building. Positive results support an original $600 million campus, a second building operating by 2013, cumulative-investment observations, and separate commitments in 2013, 2018, 2021, and 2024. The current $13 billion state claim and 2025 $9 billion multi-site commitment mix Berkeley with two Dorchester facilities and are excluded from Berkeley records.
project_updates.project_description: Google operates a multi-building data-center campus in Mount Holly Commerce Park near Moncks Corner, Berkeley County, South Carolina. The mapped inventory target is one building within that campus, so campus, company-state, later-expansion, parcel, and supporting-infrastructure values remain unallocated; the state reports the original $600 million site was established in 2007 and a second building announced in 2010 was operating by 2013. Later documented expansion announcements span 2013, 2018, 2021, 2024, and 2025.

project_updates.title: Permit and construction audit found one valued company-county permit
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: BCDCOG Construction Quarterly archive and annual reports, Berkeley County permitting/planning pages, county council packets, and exact web searches for Google Facilities, Maguro, Arum, 1669 Garrott, Mount Holly Commerce Park, and data center across 2007-2026. The only addressable Google permit value found was the December 4, 2020 $20,749,187 entry. No permit number, address, contractor, final cost, phase, hours, worker count, payroll, invoice, supplier residence, or selected-building crosswalk was public. Construction job-years therefore use a separately governed low-confidence benchmark rather than being called observed employment.

project_updates.title: Assessor audit isolated one Google-linked expansion-land account
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Berkeley County property-card search, indexed property cards, tax histories, deed/plat references, owner/address/TMS searches, and linked county GIS context. Queries included Google, Maguro Enterprises, Arum Composites, 1600 Amphitheatre, 1669/1684 Garrott, 251 Lillie, 516 Parker Simms, and TMS 211-00-02-078, -092, and -219. The live search endpoint returned a Cloudflare JavaScript challenge to noninteractive review, while indexed card 211-00-02-092 supplied exact 2024-2025 land values and paid taxes. Its acquisition note identifies five parcels bought for $25.8 million in total, but mixed deed lines prevent parcel-level allocation. Parent operating-campus, personal-property, FILOT, and full Arum/Maguro account rolls remain unresolved; former Maguro water-tank parcel -219 is now county-owned and excluded.

project_updates.title: Incentive agreement audit found legal mechanisms but no realized cost ledger
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Berkeley County Council agendas, minutes, ordinance text links, ACFRs, economic-development fund notes, Commerce Coordinating Council reports, Enterprise Zone reports, and exact searches for Maguro, Project Eagle, Project Linden, Google, fee in lieu, FILOT, special source revenue credit, multi-county park, and recapture across 2006-2025. Bills 18-45 and 20-53 confirm FILOT/credit mechanisms and amendments, but no public same-year credit used, tax avoided, cash payment, recipient receipt, clawback, or marginal service cost was found. Secondary estimates were not substituted for the missing executed schedules. The public-cost model is only an equal-cost threshold tied to one paid parcel account, not an incentive value or fiscal surplus.

project_updates.title: Water and environmental audit separates actual groundwater use from legal capacity
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: SC DES Trident groundwater evaluations, Santee basin plan, permit/public-notice portal, board minutes, wastewater and drinking-water searches, Google environmental reporting, and exact identifiers Maguro, 08IN015, 08IN015G01, 1669 Garrott, 19-RFR-48, withdrawal, discharge, stormwater, and wastewater across 2007-2025. Direct results are 2.74 million gallons of 2021 reported groundwater withdrawal and a 549 million-gallon annual permit ceiling. The DES public-notice search requires interactive state and supplied no export in this review; board minutes confirm the permit challenge was withdrawn but add no use value. Operator water-consumption values are wider reporting totals and are kept modeled/unallocated. No discharge, sewer bill, potable/reclaimed split, peak demand, meter, cooling-cycle, or selected-building allocation was public.

project_updates.title: Commissioned economic-impact outputs remain source-modeled and channel-separated
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: the full six-page Google/Deloitte South Carolina impact study, source notes, IMPLAN methodology disclosure, Google state pages, Census/BEA/BLS public series, and searches for jobs, direct employees, contractors, payroll, labor income, GDP, supplier purchases, local contractors, and household spending. The study reports 2021-2023 annual averages of approximately $626 million GDP, 6,430 jobs, and $411 million labor income, with direct/indirect/induced channels. These are reproduced only in modeled synthesis with the report's state/data-center boundary and rounding; they are not observed campus payroll, headcount, procurement, tax revenue, selected-building effects, or causal impacts. No company supplier ledger, vendor residence, local-capture share, actual payroll, benefits, or annual-average establishment FTE was public.

project_updates.title: Electricity, fuel, emissions, and cooling audit found no facility consumption ledger
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: BCWS landfill-gas page, Berkeley Electric and Santee Cooper tariffs/planning documents, Google efficiency and energy pages, SC DES air-permit/public-notice searches, EPA facility/name/address searches, and exact queries for Maguro, Google, 1669 Garrott, load, kWh, MW, PUE, generators, diesel, NOx, CO2e, and emissions across 2007-2026. The county confirms a four-year landfill-gas-credit relationship but no Google quantity or payment. The impact study reports PUE and carbon-free-energy matching at a wider data-center boundary, retained only in the exact proposal ledger. No meter, tariff assignment, bill, peak load, annual electricity, generator inventory, fuel burn, actual emissions, market-based emissions, avoided-emissions counterfactual, heat rejection, or selected-building cooling load was found; none is inferred from renewable nameplate capacity.

project_updates.title: Infrastructure and public-cost audit rejects park-wide allocation
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Berkeley County ACFRs, capital-project and debt notes, BCWS capital documents, county contract register, Mount Holly Commerce Park improvement contracts, county council records, and bond/loan searches. The ACFR describes a $500,000 annual park-revenue transfer until an approximately $4.8 million water/sewer amount and a Mount Holly pump-station loan; the contract register lists a $5,447,237 park-improvement contract. These values serve multiple park users and lack a Google beneficiary, cost-causation, service-area, reimbursement, or building allocation, so they are not project records or public-cost estimates.

project_updates.title: Recipient audit confirms one nonrecurring community grant
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Berkeley County School District, Berkeley Electric Cooperative, Home Telecom, local nonprofits, Google community pages, and the Deloitte impact study for grants, recipients, dates, purposes, and overlap. Berkeley Electric independently confirms the $250,000 Energy Advance grant. BCSD confirms iTOW and joint Google/Home Telecom support but does not isolate the vehicle amount. The 2013 greater-than-$885,000, 2019-forward approximately $500,000, and 2022-2023 approximately $2.8 million figures overlap across periods or recipients and are tagged nonadditive. No complete annual grant ledger, restricted-fund spend schedule, volunteer-hour valuation, or selected-building link was public.

project_updates.title: Metric-by-metric disposition preserves native boundaries
project_updates.notes: Investment: retained as campus cumulative observations and separate commitments. Construction: one county-reported permit retained; workers, payroll, duration, final cost, and local supplier spend remain gaps. Suppliers/household spending: only commissioned IMPLAN indirect/induced channels are modeled; no purchase ledger or residence capture is claimed. Operations: greater-than-200 people is a 2018 campus snapshot; state contribution outputs remain modeled, not headcount/payroll. Fiscal: one Arum land parcel has exact 2024-2025 values and paid taxes; campus FILOT/personal-property/receipt totals remain missing. Public costs: agreements and park infrastructure are contextual; only a same-scope equal-cost threshold is modeled. Resources: groundwater actual and permit capacity are direct; water consumption is modeled at source scope; electricity, wastewater, emissions, generators, and cooling remain gaps. Community: direct and cumulative funding is retained with overlap warnings. County GDP/employment/wage: descriptive matched comparisons are modeled with robustness checks, no causal attribution, and are not a Google effect.
